## Summary

I restructured the scattered, bare-status rejection handling so the upcoming RFC7807 change has one natural place to land, following the codebase's existing exception→`ExceptionControllerAdvice` convention. **No behaviour changed** — rejections still return the same status codes with empty bodies.

**What changed:**

1. **New `RejectedRequestException`** (`rest/advice/RejectedRequestException.java`) — a `RuntimeException` carrying the client-error `HttpStatus` (constructor + `getStatus()`). This mirrors the codebase's pattern of routing errors through the advice rather than building responses inline.

2. **`createNewOwner`** (`OwnerRestControllerV1`) — the four inline `return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST | TOO_MANY_REQUESTS | CONFLICT)` rejections now `throw new RejectedRequestException(...)`. The controller no longer builds rejection responses; its success path (201 + `Location`) is unchanged, and `addOwner`'s idempotency logic still works (rejections propagate past it, exactly as before when they were non-`CREATED` responses).

3. **New `handleRejectedRequestException`** in `ExceptionControllerAdvice` — a single `@ExceptionHandler` that maps the exception's status to a bare-status `ResponseEntity` (no body), placed alongside `handleMethodArgumentNotValidException` and reusing the same logging style as `handleDataIntegrityViolationException`.

**Why this is the right shape for the coming change:** all 400/409/429 rejection responses now converge on one advice method that already sits next to the shared `detailBuild(...)` `ProblemDetail` helper. Adding the `application/problem+json` body with `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail` will be a one-method edit there — the validation path (`handleMethodArgumentNotValidException`) already produces `ProblemDetail`, so the two rejection paths will unify cleanly rather than each rejection site needing its own body-building.

I did not implement the RFC7807 body itself, per the instructions.

I restructured the scattered, bare-status rejection handling so the upcoming RFC7807 change has one natural place to land, following the codebase's existing exception→`ExceptionControllerAdvice` convention. **No behaviour changed** — rejections still return the same status codes with empty bodies.

**What changed:**

1. **New `RejectedRequestException`** (`rest/advice/RejectedRequestException.java`) — a `RuntimeException` carrying the client-error `HttpStatus` (constructor + `getStatus()`). This mirrors the codebase's pattern of routing errors through the advice rather than building responses inline.

2. **`createNewOwner`** (`OwnerRestControllerV1`) — the four inline `return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST | TOO_MANY_REQUESTS | CONFLICT)` rejections now `throw new RejectedRequestException(...)`. The controller no longer builds rejection responses; its success path (201 + `Location`) is unchanged, and `addOwner`'s idempotency logic still works (rejections propagate past it, exactly as before when they were non-`CREATED` responses).

3. **New `handleRejectedRequestException`** in `ExceptionControllerAdvice` — a single `@ExceptionHandler` that maps the exception's status to a bare-status `ResponseEntity` (no body), placed alongside `handleMethodArgumentNotValidException` and reusing the same logging style as `handleDataIntegrityViolationException`.

**Why this is the right shape for the coming change:** all 400/409/429 rejection responses now converge on one advice method that already sits next to the shared `detailBuild(...)` `ProblemDetail` helper. Adding the `application/problem+json` body with `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail` will be a one-method edit there — the validation path (`handleMethodArgumentNotValidException`) already produces `ProblemDetail`, so the two rejection paths will unify cleanly rather than each rejection site needing its own body-building.

I did not implement the RFC7807 body itself, per the instructions.
